climate.overview_html: The most significant new quantitative assessment this cycle: the Climate Impact Lab at the University of Chicago published a pre-season mortality projection on September 23 estimating that the current Super El Niño will drive approximately 451,000 excess heat-related deaths worldwide between June 2026 and February 2027 — over and above deaths expected in an average year — with Nigeria (31,400), Indonesia (19,300) and Sudan (17,600) the most exposed countries and Africa’s Sahel the hardest-hit region overall. On the diplomatic front, Nepal’s Prime Minister used a September 25 address at UNGA to label the August 26 glacier-collapse floods “a warning to the world,” proposing a Himalaya Climate Resilience Mechanism between Nepal, India and China for shared satellite data, glacial lake monitoring and joint early warning; the speech was backed by a World Weather Attribution study released the previous week finding a “compound crisis” of warming-driven glacier retreat, permafrost thaw and geological instability — with July–August 2026 temperatures in the Langtang Lirung region approximately 1.5°C above background, attributable to human-caused climate change. The physical backdrop is unchanged: Carbon Brief’s September 25 analysis puts 2026 on track as the second-warmest year at ~1.51°C above pre-industrial, with a 92% probability that 2027 becomes the warmest year at ~1.71°C.

items.source: Climate Impact Lab / University of Chicago
items.headline: Climate Impact Lab: Super El Niño Projected to Drive 451,000 Excess Heat Deaths Worldwide June 2026–February 2027 — Nigeria 31,400 / Indonesia 19,300 / Sudan 17,600; Sahel Hardest-Hit Region; Peer-Reviewed Mortality Methodology; 239,000 Deaths in September 2026–February 2027 Window
items.summary: The Climate Impact Lab at the University of Chicago released a mortality projection on September 23 estimating that the current Super El Niño will drive approximately 451,000 excess heat-related deaths worldwide between June 2026 and February 2027 — over and above deaths expected in an average year. The methodology is peer-reviewed: it is based on a dose-response relationship between temperature and excess mortality estimated across 24,378 sub-national regions globally, calibrated for local climate vulnerability. The projection itself has not undergone peer review. Nigeria is the most exposed nation at 31,400 excess deaths, followed by Indonesia (19,300) and Sudan (17,600); Africa's Sahel is the worst-affected region. For the six-month window September 2026 through February 2027, the projection is 239,000 deaths (±11,000). The report estimates 3,500 excess deaths in the United States. The projection directly benchmarks the humanitarian cost of the Super El Niño and will be cited in UNFCCC loss-and-damage discussions ahead of COP31.

items.headline: Nepal PM at UNGA September 25: Glacier-Collapse Floods Are “Warning to World”; Proposes Himalaya Climate Resilience Mechanism (Nepal–India–China); WWA Compound-Crisis Attribution Report: ~1.5°C Human-Caused Warming in Langtang Region July–August 2026 Confirmed as Contributing Factor; 1,453+ Dead / 5,745+ Missing
items.summary: Nepal's Prime Minister addressed UNGA on September 25, framing the August 26 Langtang Lirung glacier-collapse floods — which killed at least 1,453 people and left 5,745 missing across Nepal and Tibet — as a 'warning to the world.' Nepal contributed less than one-tenth of 1% of global heat-trapping gas emissions but is paying what he called a 'colossal price.' He proposed a Himalaya Climate Resilience Mechanism to formalise satellite data sharing, glacial lake monitoring and joint early warning systems between Nepal, India and China. The speech was backed by a World Weather Attribution compound-crisis study released the prior week confirming that July-August 2026 temperatures in the Langtang Lirung region were approximately 1.5°C above background due to human-caused climate change — contributing to permafrost thaw and slope instability that primed the August 26 collapse. The WWA study gathered researchers from Nepal, UK, Ireland, Pakistan, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, the US, New Zealand and the Netherlands.

items.headline: Carbon Brief State of Climate Q3 2026 (September 25): 2026 Tracking Second-Warmest Year on Record at ~1.51°C Above Pre-Industrial; Super El Niño Drives 92% Probability 2027 Becomes Warmest Year at ~1.71°C; Jan–Aug 2026 Anomaly 0.25°C Above 2023 at Same Point
items.summary: Carbon Brief's quarterly state-of-climate analysis, published September 25, finds the January–August 2026 period tracking 1.51°C above the 1850–1900 pre-industrial baseline — approximately 0.25°C warmer than 2023 at the same point in the year. The current Super El Niño peak, with its Niño 3.4 daily anomaly reaching 3.07°C, is the primary driver. The analysis places a 92% probability on 2027 becoming the warmest year on record at a central estimate of 1.71°C above pre-industrial — the highest annual mean ever modelled — reflecting the well-documented 4–8 month lag between El Niño SST peak and global-mean temperature response.

items.headline: Copernicus C3S August 2026 Bulletin: Joint-Hottest Month on Record at 16.96°C Global-Mean Surface Temperature (1.65°C Above 1850–1900 Pre-Industrial) — First Month >1.5°C Paris Threshold Since November 2025; Western Europe JJA 2026 Hottest Summer on Record
items.summary: The Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) reported on September 10 that August 2026 tied with August 2023 as the hottest August on record at 16.96°C global-mean surface temperature — 1.65°C above the 1850–1900 pre-industrial average. This makes August 2026 the first calendar month to exceed the 1.5°C Paris Agreement threshold since November 2025. For western Europe specifically, the June–August 2026 period was the hottest summer on record, with France, Spain, Germany, and Portugal all recording their highest June–August mean temperatures.

items.headline: Super El Niño Daily Niño 3.4 Anomaly Hit 3.07°C on September 19 — Near-Tie with All-Time Daily Record (3.08°C, 19 Nov 2015) but Two Months Earlier in Calendar; Further Strengthening Forecast Through OND 2026
items.summary: Carbon Brief analysis using NOAA daily SST data finds the Niño 3.4 daily anomaly reached 3.07°C on September 19, 2026 — a statistical tie with the previous all-time daily record of 3.08°C from November 19, 2015, but arriving approximately two months earlier in the seasonal calendar. August 2026 had a monthly Niño 3.4 anomaly of approximately 2.45°C. Official forecasts continue to indicate further strengthening through October–December 2026.

items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update SON 2026: Niño 3.4 ~+3.6°C; Positive IOD +0.9°C; Above-Normal Temperatures Forecast for Most Land Areas; 2027 Still Forecast as Warmest Calendar Year on Record
items.summary: WMO's Global Seasonal Climate Update for September–November 2026 places the Niño 3.4 index at approximately +3.6°C above average, consistent with the Super El Niño at or approaching its seasonal peak. The co-occurring positive Indian Ocean Dipole at +0.9°C amplifies drought risk over Indonesia, the Philippines, and eastern Australia while increasing rainfall risk over eastern Africa and the Horn. Above-normal temperatures are forecast for most global land areas in SON 2026.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / PIK Potsdam
items.headline: GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17: “Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly” — Foster & Rahmstorf; First Statistically Confirmed Acceleration Since ~2015 at >98% Confidence; Fastest of Any Decade in 177-Year Record Across Five Temperature Datasets
items.summary: Foster and Rahmstorf apply natural-variability filtering across five global temperature datasets (NASA GISTEMP, NOAA GlobalTemp, HadCRUT5, Berkeley Earth, ERA5) to isolate the forced warming signal from ENSO, volcanic, and solar variability. The residual shows, for the first time with greater than 98% statistical confidence, that global warming has accelerated since approximately 2015 at a rate faster than any previous decade in the 177-year record. The result directly strengthens the attribution basis for the Nepal-Tibet UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission active at UNGA.

weather.overview_html: The primary operational development: the September 26 11 am PAGASA bulletin upgraded Tropical Storm Queenie (Surigae / JTWC 25W) to Severe Tropical Storm status, with maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h and gusts to 135 km/h — 5 km/h below the 115 km/h typhoon threshold — and placed the centre 575 km east-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes, tracking west-northwestward at 10 km/h; PAGASA forecasts typhoon-intensity attainment by Saturday evening, and the storm will exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility on Sunday September 27 without making landfall over any Philippine island. On the diplomatic and scientific front, Nepal’s Prime Minister used a September 25 address at UNGA to label the August 26 glacier-collapse floods a “warning to the world” and proposed a Himalaya Climate Resilience Mechanism; the WWA compound-crisis attribution study confirmed approximately 1.5°C of human-caused warming contributed to the Langtang slope failure. In the Atlantic, the 2026 hurricane-free streak has set a record not seen since 1914 — a 112-year gap — with October 8 as the sole remaining date barrier before 2026 would become only the third season since 1851 to complete without a hurricane.

items.headline: Severe Tropical Storm Queenie (Surigae / JTWC 25W) UPDATED September 26 11 AM: Upgraded from TS to STS; 110 km/h Sustained Winds / Gusts 135 km/h; 575 km ENE of Itbayat, Batanes; WNW Track; Typhoon Intensity Saturday September 26–27; Exits PAR Sunday; No Philippines Landfall
items.summary: The September 26, 2026, 11 am PAGASA bulletin upgraded Queenie (international name Surigae, JTWC 25W) from Tropical Storm to Severe Tropical Storm, with maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h near the centre and gusts to 135 km/h — 5 km/h below the 115 km/h typhoon threshold. The centre was estimated 575 km east-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes, tracking west-northwestward at 10 km/h. Sea surface temperatures of 29–30°C and low vertical wind shear are expected to support continued intensification. PAGASA forecasts typhoon-intensity attainment by Saturday evening September 26–27. The storm will exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility on Sunday September 27, passing north of the main Philippine archipelago through the sea south of Okinawa, and no Philippines landfall is forecast throughout the advisory period. Peak intensity is followed by weakening from Monday September 28.

items.headline: 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season: Zero Hurricanes Record Extended — First Time Without a Hurricane This Late Since 1914 (112-Year Gap); October 8 Is the Final Date Barrier; Completion Without Any Hurricane Would Be Only the Third Such Season Since 1851; Super El Niño Attribution Confirmed
items.summary: The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season's zero-hurricane streak has now set a record not seen since 1914 — a 112-year gap. As of September 26, six named storms have formed (all reaching only tropical storm intensity) and zero have reached hurricane strength. October 8 is the latest date in the historical record on which a season's first hurricane ever formed (1905 season); if the Atlantic remains hurricane-free through October 8, 2026 claims that record too. Should the entire season complete without a hurricane, it would be only the third such season since records began in 1851, after 1907 and 1914. Super El Niño-driven vertical wind shear across the main development region is the confirmed attribution.

items.headline: Nepal PM at UNGA: Glacier-Collapse Floods Are “Warning to World” — Proposes Himalaya Climate Resilience Mechanism (Nepal–India–China); WWA Compound-Crisis Report Confirms 1.5°C Human-Caused Warming Contributed to August 26 Langtang Slope Failure; 1,453+ Dead / 5,745+ Missing
items.summary: Nepal's Prime Minister addressed UNGA on September 25, calling the August 26 glacier-collapse disaster — which killed at least 1,453 people and left 5,745 missing across Nepal and Tibet — a 'warning to the world.' He proposed a Himalaya Climate Resilience Mechanism for shared satellite data, glacial lake monitoring and joint early warning between Nepal, India and China, noting Nepal contributed less than one-tenth of 1% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Backed by a World Weather Attribution compound-crisis study confirming that approximately 1.5°C of human-caused warming in July–August 2026 in the Langtang Lirung region contributed to permafrost thaw and slope destabilisation preceding the collapse.

items.headline: SE Asia Wildfire Haze UPDATED September 24: Philippines Government Health Advisory Active; >617,400 Fire Hotspots Detected in Indonesia (2× 2019 at Same Date); 12 Million+ People Blanketed; ASEAN Level 3 Alert; Smoke Expected Through October
items.summary: The 2026 Southeast Asian haze crisis has been ongoing since August 1, affecting Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, Singapore and Vietnam. As of September 14, more than 617,400 fire hotspots had been detected across Indonesia — more than double the number during the same period in 2019. Indonesia's Health Ministry recorded 113,336 respiratory infection cases across seven provinces on September 9. The Philippine government health advisory remains active. The ASEAN Level 3 (highest) haze alert continues. CAMS scientists project conditions will persist through October as Super El Niño suppresses the Indonesian wet-season onset.

items.headline: Europe Wildfire EFFIS Update September 24: 678,978 ha Burned as of September 23 (Up From 668,035 ha Reported September 16) — 91% Above 20-Year Average (355,397 ha) but Below 2025 Record (1,026,104 ha at Same Date)
items.summary: The European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), updated September 24 at 11:12 CEST, places the total European area burned as of September 23 at 678,978 hectares — up from the 668,035 ha reported in the prior week's bulletin, and 91% above the 20-year average (2006–2025) of 355,397 ha. The figure remains below the record 1,026,104 ha burned by September 23, 2025. The season continues to be driven by Super El Niño-amplified drought, record summer temperatures across southern and central Europe, and the Rhine at 1880-era historic low levels.

renewables.overview_html: The largest policy development this cycle: the U.S. Department of Energy announced on September 24 that it will provide $1.9 billion in federal funding to 31 grid-improvement projects across 26 states under the SPARK (Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and Key Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades) initiative; recipient cost-share brings total investment to $5.25 billion; the upgrades will reconductor or rebuild more than 1,500 miles of transmission lines and deploy Grid-Enhancing Technologies across 21,000 miles, unlocking more than 23 GW of additional grid capacity for approximately 100 million Americans. From the prior 72-hour window: Fluence announced a 206 GWh multi-year battery supply framework with EVE Energy for 2027–2031, one of the largest long-term BESS supply commitments in the utility-scale storage industry; and WindEnergy Hamburg 2026 closed September 25 after four days with 1,600+ exhibitors and 43,000 participants, with Europe-wide CfD indexation for offshore wind as the dominant policy theme.

items.source: U.S. Department of Energy / TD World
items.headline: DOE Announces $1.9 Billion Federal Funding ($5.25 Billion Total with Cost-Share) for 31 Grid-Improvement Projects Across 26 States Under SPARK Initiative — 1,500+ Miles Reconductored; 23 GW Capacity Unlocked; 21,000 Miles of Grid-Enhancing Technology Deployment
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Electricity announced on September 24, 2026 the selection of 31 grid-improvement projects across 26 states under the SPARK initiative. $1.9 billion in federal funding plus $3.35 billion in recipient cost-share brings total investment to $5.25 billion. Projects will reconductor or rebuild more than 1,500 miles of transmission lines using advanced conductors and deploy Grid-Enhancing Technologies across nearly 21,000 miles of existing lines, unlocking more than 23 GW of additional capacity — equivalent to powering approximately 17 million homes — for roughly 100 million Americans without building new transmission corridors. Formal financial-assistance agreements are expected between October 2026 and January 2027.

items.headline: Fluence — EVE Energy 206 GWh Multi-Year Battery Supply Framework 2027–2031 — Utility-Scale BESS Systems; EVE-3 Cylindrical Cell Technology; One of Largest Long-Term BESS Supply Commitments in Industry
items.summary: Fluence announced on September 24 a multi-year battery supply framework agreement with EVE Energy covering 206 GWh of utility-scale battery energy storage systems from 2027 through 2031. The deal secures EVE's new EVE-3 large-format cylindrical cell technology, to be deployed in Fluence's Gridstack and Ultrastack BESS platforms. The 206 GWh five-year commitment covers approximately 5 GW of estimated projects and is one of the largest long-term BESS supply frameworks in the utility-scale storage industry.

items.headline: RWE at WindEnergy Hamburg September 22: Calls for Europe-Wide CfD Indexation for Offshore Wind; Up to €4.4 Billion in Savings for Germany’s 9 GW Pipeline by 2030; €2 Billion Savings for 4 GW Tendered in 2027
items.summary: RWE's head of offshore wind development called at WindEnergy Hamburg on September 22 for Europe-wide adoption of indexation for offshore wind Contracts for Difference, linking strike prices to inflation indices over the operating term. For Germany's 4 GW planned for tendering in 2027, potential cost reductions are estimated at up to €2 billion; for Germany's full 9 GW tender pipeline through 2030, up to €4.4 billion.

items.headline: CTUIL Releases TSA for 2 GW Solapur Renewable Energy Evacuation and Transmission Expansion Project (India) — 10-Day Window to Execute and Acquire 100% SPV Equity; Part of India’s 500 GW Renewable Target Grid Reinforcement
items.summary: Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd (CTUIL) released a Transmission Service Agreement on September 23 for a 2 GW renewable energy evacuation and transmission expansion project in Solapur, Maharashtra. The selected bidder has 10 days to execute the TSA and pay the acquisition price for 100% equity in the Special Purpose Vehicle. The project is part of India's grid reinforcement program to evacuate power from the Solapur solar and wind zones — a critical bottleneck for India's 500 GW renewable target by 2030.

items.headline: 50Hertz Awards LanWin3 2 GW North Sea HVDC Converter Platform to NSORe + Siemens Energy — Second 2 GW NSORe/50Hertz Contract in 2026; Combined LanWin3 + LanWin6 Value ~€2.5 Billion
items.summary: German TSO 50Hertz awarded the LanWin3 North Sea offshore HVDC converter platform contract to the NSORe JV and Siemens Energy on September 18. This is NSORe's second major 50Hertz contract in 2026, following LanWin6 in June. Combined NSORe value for LanWin3 and LanWin6 totals approximately €2.5 billion.

items.headline: LS Marine Solution Wins 156.9 Billion Won (~US$114 M) Submarine Cable Contract for 390 MW Sinan Wooi Offshore Wind Farm — South Korea’s First National Growth Fund Project; First in 8.2 GW Sinan Belt
items.summary: LS Marine Solution secured a 156.9 billion Korean won (~US$114 million) contract on September 18 to supply and install submarine power cables for the 390 MW Sinan Wooi offshore wind farm — its largest-ever order at 2.2× its full-year FY2025 revenue. Sinan Wooi is the first project to receive funding from South Korea's National Growth Fund for offshore wind and the opening project in the government-designated 8.2 GW Sinan offshore wind development belt.

science.overview_html: Two new papers extend the ML weather model landscape this cycle. Aries (arXiv:2609.13292) — from InCommodities, a private energy trading firm — demonstrates that a SwinTransformer-based MLWP model built entirely within a commercial energy organisation at 0.25° / 74 prognostic variables outperforms ECMWF HRES on 10-metre wind speed RMSE at lead times up to 4 days and matches AIFS on 2-metre temperature, establishing that competitive ML NWP can now be deployed by private sector energy actors without reliance on national meteorological service infrastructure. Lightweight Probabilistic Downscaling from a Deterministic Base Model (arXiv:2609.29383, September 24) introduces a two-stage training curriculum combining deterministic pretraining with probabilistic tuning on a U-Net backbone, beating state-of-the-art RMSE on the CORDEX-ML-Bench suite for daily maximum temperature and precipitation across three regions (Alps, New Zealand, South Africa) at substantially reduced computational cost. The leading ERA5 cold-bias finding — Landsberg & Barnes (GRL, September 24) showing a systematic ~0.035°C/decade cold bias in AIFS, GraphCast and Pangu-Weather forecasts inherited from ERA5 training data — remains the most operationally urgent result, directly affecting how AI model temperature output should be interpreted for attribution and verification.

items.headline: Aries (arXiv:2609.13292) — Proprietary SwinTransformer ML Weather Model for Energy Industry at 0.25° / 74 Variables; Outperforms ECMWF HRES on 10m Wind Speed RMSE at <4 Days; Matches AIFS on 2m Temperature; Competitive ML NWP Now Reachable by Commercial Energy Sector
items.summary: Aries is a SwinTransformer-based machine-learned weather prediction (MLWP) model developed by InCommodities, a private energy trading company, and trained on ERA5 reanalysis data at 0.25° resolution predicting 74 prognostic and 11 diagnostic atmospheric variables. Evaluated on 2025 ECMWF Analysis initializations (strictly out-of-sample), Aries outperforms ECMWF HRES on 10-metre wind speed RMSE for lead times up to four days — directly relevant to wind energy operations — while achieving 2-metre temperature RMSE on par with ECMWF AIFS. The paper demonstrates that competitive ML NWP capabilities can now be built, trained, and deployed by commercial energy-sector organisations without dependence on academic or national meteorological service infrastructure, opening the door to energy-tailored model variants that optimise for wind and solar forecast skill.

items.headline: Lightweight Probabilistic Downscaling from a Deterministic Base Model (arXiv:2609.29383) — Two-Stage Curriculum (Deterministic Pretraining + Probabilistic Tuning) on U-Net Backbone; Beats State-of-the-Art RMSE on CORDEX-ML-Bench (Alps, NZ, South Africa); Daily Tmax and Precipitation
items.meta: McLean, Vlaar, Passano Hellan, Ericsson · arXiv:2609.29383 [cs.LG] · Submitted 24 September 2026
items.summary: McLean et al. introduce a lightweight approach to probabilistic climate downscaling, adapting two methods on a modified U-Net backbone trained with a two-stage curriculum combining deterministic pretraining with probabilistic tuning. Evaluated on the CORDEX-ML-Bench suite for daily maximum temperature and precipitation across three geographic regions — the Alps, New Zealand and South Africa — the approach beats state-of-the-art RMSE while remaining computationally accessible. The result reduces the trade-off between computational intensity and distributional fit that has constrained probabilistic downscaling at high resolution, making ensemble high-resolution projections more accessible for regional climate services and impact assessors.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / Colorado State University
items.headline: GRL: AI Weather Model 2-m Temperature Forecasts Carry 15–20-Year Cold Bias From ERA5 Training Data — Landsberg & Barnes (CSU / GRL 2026); ~0.035°C/Decade Systematic Underestimate in ECMWF AIFS, GraphCast, Pangu-Weather; Bias Correction Required Before Climate Attribution
items.meta: Landsberg & Barnes · Colorado State University · Geophysical Research Letters (2026) · Published 24 September 2026
items.summary: Landsberg and Barnes evaluate 2-metre temperature forecasts from ECMWF AIFS, Google DeepMind GraphCast, and Huawei Pangu-Weather, identifying a systematic cold bias of approximately 0.035°C per decade inherited from the ERA5 reanalysis training corpus. Because ERA5 spans 1940–2024, models trained on it produce 2-m temperature anomalies calibrated against a baseline 15–20 years of warming behind the present day. All three models show consistent negative temperature bias growing with forecast lead time. The study concludes these models are unsuitable for near-real-time climate attribution or warming-trend estimation without explicit post-processing bias correction and calls for training dataset refreshes or dynamic climatology normalisation as standard practice.

items.headline: HClimRep-Ocean (arXiv:2609.28601) — First Transformer Ocean Emulator on FESOM2 Unstructured Mesh; Full 3D Reconstruction Including Sea Ice, Salinity, SSH; State-of-the-Art vs. ClimaX and FourCastNet Ocean Baselines at 1–12-Month Horizons
items.summary: HClimRep-Ocean introduces the first transformer-based ocean emulator operating on FESOM2's native unstructured triangular mesh, avoiding regridding artifacts from mapping irregular ocean grids to structured lat-lon grids. Variables include 3D temperature and salinity at 24 depth levels, sea surface height, and sea ice concentration and thickness. The model achieves state-of-the-art skill scores versus ClimaX ocean fine-tune and FourCastNet ocean baselines across all variables at 1–12-month prediction horizons. The unstructured-mesh capability is particularly significant for accurately representing coastal upwelling zones and polar ocean processes.

items.headline: FAST-ML (arXiv:2609.25505) — Hybrid Physics–ML Framework for Tropical Cyclone Intensity Forecasting; Dual-Stream ERA5 Neural Parameterization Coupled to Differentiable FAST Intensity Model; End-to-End Optimization for Rapid Intensification
items.meta: Xiao, Lin, Ehrmann, Sarhadi · arXiv:2609.25505 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 22 September 2026
items.summary: FAST-ML bridges data-driven efficiency with physical constraints for tropical cyclone intensity forecasting, targeting rapid intensification. A physically-informed dual-stream neural parameterization ingests 3D ERA5 atmospheric fields to diagnose ventilation controls (environmental wind shear and mid-level entropy deficit), fed into a differentiable implementation of the FAST intensity model with end-to-end optimization. Directly relevant to Severe Tropical Storm Queenie (25W) intensity guidance as it approaches typhoon threshold.

items.headline: Sparse-Observation Atmospheric Thermal Forecasting With PINNs for Climate-Aware Digital Twins (arXiv:2609.27290) — Chegini et al.; RMSE Improvement 8.1% at 1-Hour to 23.8% at 3-Hour Lead vs. Baselines; Oklahoma ERA5 Case Study
items.meta: Chegini, Shivanian, Karimi, Dadgostari · arXiv:2609.27290 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 23 September 2026
items.summary: Evaluates a physics-informed neural network constrained by a pressure-coordinate thermodynamic advection-source equation for short-horizon (1–3 hour) atmospheric temperature forecasts at sparse-observation locations, achieving mean RMSE improvement growing from 8.1% at one hour to 23.8% at three hours. Supports climate-aware digital twin use cases for built-environment operations, smart grids, and wildfire risk platforms requiring hyperlocal thermal forecasts in data-sparse regions.

items.headline: Transfer Learning for Atmospheric Transport Emulators (arXiv:2609.23838) — Clark et al. (U Bristol); LPDM Emulator Extended from South America to Four Global Regions; ~1,000× Faster Than Physics-Based Model; Enables High-Resolution Satellite GHG Inversion at Scale
items.meta: Clark, Fillola, Keshtmand, Santos-Rodriguez, Rigby · arXiv:2609.23838 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 20 September 2026 · University of Bristol
items.summary: Evaluates whether a high-performance Lagrangian Particle Dispersion Model emulator — running approximately 1,000× faster than the UK Met Office's NAME LPDM — can be spatially transferred to new regions via transfer learning. The authors evaluate transferability across four world regions, establishing conditions for extending the emulator without full retraining. Opens a pathway toward global, high-resolution greenhouse gas inversion from modern satellite instruments (OCO-2, TROPOMI) at previously unaffordable costs.

items.headline: TAISE: AI-Driven Catastrophe Risk Modeling via Emergent Scenario Generation (arXiv:2609.16493) — Hang Gao; 50-Year Simulation on One GPU for US$130 with 2,000+ Cyclonic Events; Order-of-Magnitude Cost Reduction vs. Traditional CAT Models
items.summary: TAISE repurposes AI weather forecasting models to generate coherent continuous global atmospheric fields via self-iterative rollout, from which extreme events emerge rather than being manually constructed. A proof-of-concept 50-year simulation on a single GPU cost approximately US$130 and produced more than 2,000 cyclonic events — an order-of-magnitude reduction in computational cost versus conventional catastrophe modelling. Directly applicable to the reinsurance and ILS sector, which has seen five consecutive years of global insured nat-cat losses exceeding US$100 billion.

items.headline: WeatherNext 3 (arXiv:2609.03582) — Google DeepMind: Operational Hourly Global Probabilistic Forecasts at 0.1° via Raw Geostationary Satellite Ingestion; Functional Generative Networks on Multiresolution Icosahedral Mesh; Powers Google Search + Google Maps
items.meta: Google DeepMind + Google Research · arXiv:2609.03582 [cs.LG] · Submitted 3 September 2026 · Operational
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 generates new probabilistic forecasts every hour by ingesting low-latency geostationary satellite imagery directly, achieving 0.1° spatial resolution while eliminating the 6-hour analysis lag that constrains traditional AI model architectures. Architecture: Functional Generative Networks operating on a multiresolution icosahedral mesh. Now operationally deployed by Google, powering weather data in Google Search and Google Maps.

items.title: DOE SPARK Initiative Selects 31 US Grid Projects for $1.9 Billion Federal Funding ($5.25 Billion Total with Cost-Share) — 1,500+ Miles Reconductored; 23 GW Unlocked Without New Corridors; 21,000 Miles of Grid-Enhancing Technology Deployment Across 26 States
items.body_html: The U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Electricity announced on September 24 the selection of 31 grid-improvement projects across 26 states under the SPARK initiative, with $1.9 billion in federal funding and $3.35 billion in recipient cost-share for a total of $5.25 billion. Projects will reconductor or rebuild more than 1,500 miles of transmission lines and deploy Grid-Enhancing Technologies across nearly 21,000 miles of existing lines, unlocking more than 23 GW of additional capacity — for roughly 100 million Americans — without requiring new transmission corridors; formal financial-assistance agreements are expected between October 2026 and January 2027.

items.title: Fortune / PitchBook: Climate Tech VC Fund Fundraising Fell ~40% in H1 2026 Despite Record Investment Totals — AI Data Centre Demand Filling Gap Left by Pure-Climate Funds; Bifurcation Sharpening Between AI-Adjacent and Traditional Climate-Only Verticals
items.body_html: Fortune, citing PitchBook LP fundraising data, reported on September 23 that climate-tech-dedicated VC fund formation fell approximately 40% in H1 2026 by capital raised compared to H1 2025 — even as total climate-tech investment reached a record $26.1 billion in the same period. The paradox reflects AI-infrastructure demand for firm low-carbon power being increasingly funded by generalist and growth funds that do not self-identify as “climate VC.” PitchBook’s analysis finds the 10 largest H1 2026 climate deals drew on sovereign wealth funds, Big Tech corporate VC and pension capital — potentially hollowing out the early-stage climate pipeline if LPs continue to withdraw from pure-play climate fund vehicles.

items.title: Kairos Power Secures Up to $100 Million from Samsung C&T for Google Hermes 2 Nuclear Reactor Build — $70 M Equity + $30 M In-Kind Engineering; 50 MW Fluoride Salt-Cooled Demonstration Plant at Oak Ridge; Operations Target 2030
items.body_html: Kairos Power and Samsung C&T agreed on September 21 to a binding term sheet under which Samsung C&T will provide up to $100 million — $70 million equity plus $30 million in-kind engineering — to support the delivery of the 50 MW fluoride salt-cooled Hermes 2 Demonstration Plant in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. Hermes 2 is purpose-built to supply firm low-carbon baseload power for Google’s AI data centres; Samsung C&T brings direct reactor construction execution capability across approximately a dozen nuclear projects globally.
items.source_html: TechCrunch / World Nuclear News

items.title: Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B for Drone-Based Cloud Seeding — Led by NOA VC + Upfront; DCVC, Lowercarbon, Dream Ventures Co-Invest; Targets Drought Relief in American West and Data Center Water Demand
items.body_html: Rainmaker, the El Segundo weather-modification startup, announced a $100 million Series B on September 21 led by NOA VC and Upfront Ventures, with co-investment from DCVC, Lowercarbon Capital and Dream Ventures — bringing total funding to $150.3 million since its 2023 founding. Rainmaker deploys drone fleets to seed clouds with silver iodide, framing cloud seeding as climate adaptation targeting drought relief in the American West and humidification services for water-hungry hyperscale data centres.

items.title: CTVC / Currence H1’26 Climate Tech Report: $26.1 Billion Global VC in H1 2026 (+55% YoY); Data Centers 34% of Total; Deal Count at 5-Year Low (-25%); Series A up 55% to $4.5 Bn; Adaptation Funding +64% — Fastest-Growing Sub-Vertical
items.body_html: CTVC (now Currence) published its H1’26 Climate Tech Investment Report on September 21, finding total global venture investment reached $26.1 billion in H1 2026 — up 55% year-on-year — driven overwhelmingly by data-centre infrastructure. The Built Environment category grew more than 800% and overtook Energy as the largest funding vertical, with deal count falling 25% to a 5-year low; the 10 largest rounds taking 42% of all H1 2026 investment; Series A rising 55% to $4.5 billion; and adaptation funding growing 64% — the fastest-growing sub-vertical.

items.title: NOAA NESDIS Awards $67 Million to Spire Global, PlanetiQ, and Ethereal Space for Commercial GNSS-RO Data — 10,000 Daily Radio-Occultation Profiles for NWP and Space-Weather Monitoring; Multi-Year Operational Contracts Through 2029
items.body_html: NOAA NESDIS announced on September 18 awards totalling $67 million to Spire Global, PlanetiQ and Ethereal Space for operational GNSS radio-occultation data contracts running through 2029. The contracts deliver approximately 10,000 radio-occultation soundings per day, nearly doubling the operational GNSS-RO input to NOAA’s Global Forecast System. Ethereal Space receives its first NOAA operational contract, providing specialized polar-orbit coverage relevant to Arctic sea-ice and polar vortex monitoring — direct inputs to the AI weather models tracked in the Science & Research section.

items.title: Cat Bond and ILS Market Bulletin (Week Ending September 20): MembersCap Launches First Cat Bond Fund + Novel ILW; Gallagher Securities Developing First-Ever New-Peril Cat Bond; CalPERS ILS Holdings Approach US$2.5 Billion; Record $11 Billion Q2 2026 Issuance; Artemis London 2026 Closes
items.body_html: The Artemis weekly bulletin for the week ending September 20 highlights: MembersCap launched the first dedicated cat bond fund strategy alongside a novel ILW structure; Gallagher Securities is developing the first-ever cat bond covering a previously unbondable peril; and CalPERS’ ILS holdings are approaching US$2.5 billion at mid-year 2026 — the fifth consecutive year of global insured nat-cat losses exceeding US$100 billion and Q2 2026 posting a record $11 billion in cat bond issuance. Artemis London 2026 also concluded this week with the consensus finding that the cat bond market is well-positioned for disciplined, continued growth.

items.title: Mazama Energy Raises $135 Million Series B for Superhot Engineered Geothermal — Led by Centaurus Capital + Doerr Capital; ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla, Gates Frontier Co-Invest; Project Athena Targeting 750°F (400°C) at Newberry Volcano, Oregon
items.body_html: Mazama Energy raised $135 million in an oversubscribed Series B announced September 17, co-led by Centaurus Capital and Doerr Capital, with ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Gates Frontier and others participating. Mazama holds the record for the hottest EGS ever built — 629°F (331°C) at Newberry Volcano in 2025; Project Athena targets 750°F (400°C), where a single well can deliver up to 10× the power of a conventional 390°F well using 75% less water and 80% fewer wells.

items.title: EU Climate Insurance Alliance — Von der Leyen State of the Union September 16: Only 25% of European Catastrophe Losses Currently Insured; Parametric + Group Instruments Proposed; 100 Vulnerable EU Regions Mapped by October; Alliance Faces Criticism for Lacking Mandatory Cover Mandate
items.body_html: European Commission President von der Leyen announced the European Climate Insurance Alliance in her September 16 State of the Union address, citing data showing only 25% of European catastrophic climate losses are currently insured. The Alliance will develop group insurance pools for uninsurable catastrophe risks and expand parametric instruments for agriculture, coastal flooding and wildfire; the European Commission will map the 100 most-vulnerable EU regions by October 2026. The announcement follows Europe’s wildfire season reaching 678,978 ha per EFFIS, with uninsured losses estimated at €40–60 billion. Critics noted the Alliance would not close the protection gap without a mandatory natural-hazard cover mandate.
items.source_html: Green Central Banking / The Insurer
